setlist.title: Beat It On Down The Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Cat Sunflower** (3 reviews): Second-set China>Rider shows subtle interplay between Lesh and Garcia; Opening set two with China>Rider is called among the best of the eighties [7][12][13]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): The cut Stranger wails, and the whole first set sizzles [12]
- **They Love Each Other** (1 review): Reviewer calls it the best version ever, with Lesh and Garcia interplaying intensely and Garcia taking a long, inventive solo [7]
- **New Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Reviewer says Lesh plays outstandingly on Minglewood [13]
- **Brokedown Palace** (1 other source): Fades in because of a very loud buzz [2]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-06-10.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.105976.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 140 min; rated 3.55/5 by 11 [1]
- **gd1984-06-10.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.77323.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 139 min; rated 3.17/5 by 6 [2]
- **gd84-06-10.sbd.willy.10163.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 133 min; rated 4.58/5 by 12 [5]. Said about its sound: Soundboard is well balanced and captures Lesh in an energetic mood; Soundboard sounds tight and slightly sped up, though the band is simply jamming hard; Reviewer checked against a keyboard and found the tape definitely runs fast, most noticeably on China Cat-Rider [7][10][11]
- **gd1984-06-10.beyerm160.quirk.perez.32366.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 17 songs; 118 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [6]. Said about its sound: Front-of-board-area audience recording: crisp, close, good bottom end, little crowd noise, some hiss [6]

## Around the show

- Daytime Cal Expo heat was overwhelming; outdoor showers behind the bleachers were the main relief [8]
- Garcia looked about as unwell as he ever did around this time; a first-timer friend asked a question about the band [8]
- No Garcia ballad follows space, which may hint at his condition; tempo is energetic [14]
- Attendee bought a tie-dye on the back fence; watched from top of bleacher stairs in spring sunshine [15]
- Garcia appeared to have a greenish hue to his skin at the time [15]
- Attendee taped both days; Garcia's playing this day was sloppy with mistakes [18]
- Playing is fast even for the band, and Garcia is outstanding by 1984 standards [11]
- Feels like a rowdy Centrum or Garden show rather than a typical outdoor date [12]
- Band plays at a very fast tempo; the 21 July show is similar [13]
- Reviewer prefers the October 1984 Maine and Hartford shows as the year's best [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-06-10.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.105976.flac16**: taped by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Nakamichi 550/Maxell XLIIS-90) [1]. Also: Source tapes came from Joani Walker and Paul Scotton, with pitch correction help from Joe B. Jones [1]
- **gd1984-06-10.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.77323.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Nakamichi 550/Maxell XLIIS-90) D [2]. Also: Cassettes from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker; a tape flip during drums was smoothed with a crossfade [2]
- **gd84-06-10.sbd.willy.10163.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by EAC/SHN by Willy; source: SBD>MC>C>DAT>CDR [5]
- **gd1984-06-10.beyerm160.quirk.perez.32366.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Jim Quirk; transferred by Jim Quirk and David Perez; source: 2Beyer M160s>D5>MC [6]. Also: Taped by Jim Quirk using Beyer M160 mics; seed discs came from him [6]
